name: Jowai Town
description: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district and cultural hub of the Pnar (Jaintia) people, situated on a plateau at about 1365 m elevation surrounded by the Myntdu River.
facts: Commercial and educational centre for the region

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning multi-tiered waterfall near Amlarem with vivid turquoise-blue pool formed by mineral-rich limestone water, surrounded by dense forest. Popular for swimming and photography.
facts: Entry fee around Rs 50; life jackets available
Best in dry season for clearest water
Short trek of 15-20 minutes from parking

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest collection of megalithic monoliths (menhirs and dolmens) in Meghalaya, erected between 16th-19th centuries by Jaintia kings and clans as memorials. Includes the tallest menhir in the state.

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: Ancient 600-year-old Durga temple, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, with unique fusion of Hindu and local Jaintia traditions. Historically associated with the Jaintia kingdom.
facts: Site of annual Durga Puja celebrations

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake (also called Pung Sajar Nangli) near Mukhla village, created according to legend by followers of rebel general Sajar Nangli using bow tips. Popular picnic and boating spot.
facts: About 8-13 km from Jowai on NH6
Scenic views and paddle boats available

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic multi-stage waterfall near Jowai on the Shillong-Jowai road, cascading over cliffs with views of paddy fields. Accessible via short walk over an arch bridge.
facts: Best viewed from upper and lower points

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Riverside meadow on the banks of the Myntdu River meaning 'Golden Flower'. Historical site linked to freedom fighter U Kiang Nangbah; popular local picnic and angling spot with suspension bridge.
facts: Named from local folklore of a golden flower

name: Ialong Park
description: Ecological park about 8 km from Jowai overlooking the Pynthorwah Valley and Myntdu River. Features sacred groves, walking trails, viewpoints, and ongoing eco-tourism development.

name: Dawki and Umngot River
description: Border town on the India-Bangladesh frontier famous for the crystal-clear Umngot (Dawki) River where the riverbed is visible. Iconic 1932 suspension bridge and boat rides.
facts: About 40 km from Jowai, 90+ km from Shillong

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Village upstream on the Umngot River offering quieter clear-water experiences, camping, kayaking, cliff jumping and ziplining compared to busier Dawki.

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Secluded multi-tiered waterfall with clear turquoise plunge pool, requiring a moderate trek through forest and rural paths. Less crowded hidden gem near Jarain/Shkentalang area.
facts: Suitable for swimming in the pool

name: Thlu Muwi
description: Historic site with a traditional stone bridge made of large intricately carved granite slabs supported by pillars, adjacent to Muwi Waterfalls. Located along the Jowai-Dawki road.

name: Khliehriat Town
description: Headquarters of East Jaintia Hills district, a mining and transit hub on the plateau with Pnar cultural influences, government facilities, and access to surrounding caves and waterfalls.
facts: District created in 2012 from Jaintia Hills

name: Moopun Waterfalls and Stone Bridge
description: Scenic waterfall on the Umjhai River at Mutong village dropping about 110 feet into a sandy pool, topped by a traditional stone bridge and natural swimming pool. Features rare pitcher plants on the rocks.
facts: About 25 km equidistant from Jowai and Khliehriat
Linked by legend to Umhang Lake

name: Umhang Lake
description: Largest natural lake in the Jaintia Hills, located at Bataw village and surrounded by dense forest. Revered locally with a legend of formation from a spring scratched by an old woman of the Suchiang clan.

name: Krem Liat Prah
description: Longest natural cave in India and South Asia (explored length about 34 km and growing) on the Shnongrim Ridge. Features massive chambers including the Aircraft Hangar trunk passage; expedition caving only with guides.
facts: One of ~150 caves on Shnongrim Ridge
Aircraft Hangar is a vast trunk passage
Best October to April; avoid monsoon flooding

name: Borghat Temple
description: Historic brick temple dedicated to Lord Shiva in Borghat (Shilliangpusi) village, built by early Jaintia rulers who embraced Hinduism. Features unique carvings and stands near the old Borkhat Palace ruins.
facts: One of the earliest Hindu temples in the region

name: Rynji Falls
description: Powerful waterfall in Cham Cham village area on rocky terrain, creating a dramatic cascade. Requires a moderate walk from the nearest road and borders West Jaintia Hills.

name: Umbyrlein Falls
description: Iconic waterfall at Rangad village, offering scenic views and a relatively accessible nature spot in the district.

name: Sahksaw Fish Sanctuary
description: Tranquil community fish sanctuary at Cham Cham village, a picturesque spot for observing aquatic life in clear waters amid rural surroundings.
facts: About 700 metres from Cham Cham village centre

name: Tisang River
description: Scenic river near Borghat village flowing through forests and villages, popular for riverside camping and adventure activities.
facts: Approached from Borghat about 50 km from Khliehriat

name: Lukha River and Bridge
description: Scenic stretch of the Lukha River at Sonapur with the district's longest concrete arch bridge, connecting to eastern Assam and offering mountain and landscape views as it flows toward Bangladesh.

name: Moolamylliang Village
description: Village in Saipung block offering adventure, natural scenery and recreational experiences in a relatively unexplored rural setting of East Jaintia Hills.
facts: Listed for adventure and scenic beauty
